summary: no real engine matches the Carnot cycle; a reviewer's job is to say how far short we are. v2 wins the narrow fail-open argument by keeping exactly one room, but that victory burns away the premise: the remaining island design is a best-effort occupancy label with a new table, new endpoints, new webhook surface, new key prerequisite, and no authority over the call. Dijkstra: "Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability." The simpler reversible path is increment 0: signed call-ended messages in app history, keep the existing video-token path, and do zero island work until a feature truly needs an authoritative server-side call object.
fatal_flaws: The design claims to preserve "a call as a first-class object," but deletes the object on end, keeps history elsewhere, keeps media identity as the channel, and forbids the row from deciding any capability. That is not first-class objecthood; it is an ephemeral occupancy cache with a ULID.

The remaining table does not earn its thermodynamic cost. If `live` is never a gate and joining always uses the existing channel room, stale false and stale true are both tolerated by contract. The row can only color UI and count participants, so the island absorbs schema, API, cascade, webhook, TTL, and privacy blast radius for information the design itself says must not be trusted.

The zombie-participant counter-case is not merely carried; it is the core failure left standing. One eternal room means stale participants, frozen tiles, reconnect ghosts, and no per-call clean slate. Saying it is not a regression is not a design argument; it is an admission that #3170's room half was solving a real state-contamination problem v2 abandons.

The reversal of #3170 is under-justified. Objecthood and per-call room are separable in theory, but here the per-call room was the only mechanism that gave irreversibility to a media session. Feynman: "What I cannot create, I do not understand." v2 names a call but cannot create a distinct media event, close one, or prevent residue from one from appearing in the next.

The webhook/key prerequisite remains disproportionate. Per-island LiveKit keys plus a public authenticated webhook endpoint may be rational for authoritative call lifecycle, but v2 explicitly demotes lifecycle to advisory UI state. That is entropy production without useful work.

The `POST /calls` unique index is not harmless; it can still make the recorded call identity diverge from signed history under glare. The design says that is acceptable because history is authoritative elsewhere. Then the recorded identity is not authoritative enough to justify existing.

`GET /call` as #3159 replacement is weaker than advertised. #3159 wanted to answer whether the callee is still being rung for the same event. v2 cannot distinguish call epochs in the SFU and intentionally refuses to gate on the answer. It returns a soft presence hint, not the semantic liveness #3159 was reaching for.

The open variables are not peripheral. `departureTimeout`, `empty_reap`, `max_duration`, takedown behavior, webhook placement, and explicit end endpoint together define the actual lifecycle. A design whose core is lifecycle cannot leave its lifecycle as open variables and still be considered cast.
what_holds: Fail-open is no longer the round-1 catastrophe: with only `room_for_channel`, both honest parties join the same room even if `POST /calls` or `GET /call` fails.
Keeping `POST /v1/channels/{id}/video-token` unchanged is correct. The live nine-round trust boundary should not be rewritten for an advisory record.
The client must still treat the LiveKit room as opaque and receive it only from the token response.
Signed invite and signed end messages are the right durable history substrate. They federate, carry attribution, and avoid inventing a local CDR.

DM-only on the mutator, count-only participants, 404 for existence hiding, `no-store`, and "live is a label, never a gate" are all sound local constraints if this design proceeds despite the larger objection.
fold_back: DISSOLVE the island half for now: ship increment 0 in the app tab as a signed call-ended sentinel over existing message history, with no island schema or endpoint change.
Keep the existing `POST /v1/channels/{id}/video-token` path and channel room. Do not add `live_calls` until a caller can name a server-side decision that must be authoritative.

If occupancy is still wanted later, recast it honestly as an advisory presence feature, not "a call as a first-class object." Price it against LiveKit-native presence behavior, privacy exposure, and webhook/key work.

If the product requirement is clean media sessions, return to per-call rooms and solve federation/keying explicitly; do not pretend an eternal room plus a deleted row gives the same thermodynamic boundary.
Hamming: "The purpose of computing is insight, not numbers." The insight here is that once the row is forbidden from controlling anything, the computation is mostly waste heat.
